source.note: hand-written; a migration gotcha in a TypeScript + Postgres project called ledgerly

units.text: The orders report is timing out. I think we need an index on orders(customer_id, created_at). Write the migration. Naming convention is <timestamp>_<snake_description>.ts like the others in db/migrations.

Some background on why this helps: a B-tree index on (customer_id, created_at) lets Postgres satisfy both the equality filter on customer_id and the range or ORDER BY on created_at from the index alone, instead of scanning the heap and sorting. Column order matters: equality columns first, then the range column. Postgres can also use the leading column alone, so this index serves customer_id-only queries too.

I will write it as `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` since the table is live.
Yes, definitely concurrently. orders has about 40 million rows in production and a plain CREATE INDEX would lock writes for several minutes. We got burned by that in December.

Wrote db/migrations/20260304_add_orders_customer_created_idx.ts. Running it locally failed, though: `ERROR: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block`. The project's migration runner (db/run-migrations.ts) wraps every migration in BEGIN/COMMIT. Postgres forbids CONCURRENTLY inside a transaction because the build has to wait for other transactions in multiple phases.

Looked at the runner: it already supports an escape hatch. A migration module can export `disableTransaction = true` and the runner then executes it with autocommit. Added that export to the new migration, re-ran locally, and the index built. Also confirmed with EXPLAIN that the report query now does an Index Scan on the new index instead of a Seq Scan plus Sort.
Perfect. Put a comment at the top of the migration saying why disableTransaction is there, so nobody deletes it thinking it's a leftover.
Added the comment: "CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction; the runner wraps migrations in one unless this flag is set." The migration file is complete and the local database has the index.

expected.content: In ledgerly, the migration runner wraps every migration in a transaction; a migration that uses CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY must export disableTransaction = true or it fails with 'cannot run inside a transaction block'.
The orders table has about 40 million rows in production, so indexes must be built CONCURRENTLY; a plain CREATE INDEX locked writes for minutes in December 2025.
An index on orders(customer_id, created_at) was added in March 2026 to fix the orders report timing out.
Migration files are named <timestamp>_<snake_description>.ts under db/migrations.
